login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb.

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

oidc_jwt.description: When no `resource` is included in the authorization/token request, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: This is by design and should not be flagged as missing JWT claims or audience-binding failure.

oidc_jwt.description: If a default API resource is configured, Logto uses it as the audience when `resource` is omitted in authentication requests.
oidc_jwt.note: A token for the default audience after omitting `resource` is expected behavior, not audience confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, refreshed tokens cannot include scopes that were not requested in the original authorization flow.
oidc_jwt.note: Lack of newly granted scopes on refresh is by design, not an authorization bug.

oidc_jwt.description: If organization_id is omitted, only global roles and permissions are evaluated; organization RBAC is not enforced.
oidc_jwt.note: A token lacking organization enforcement is expected when no organization context was requested.

oidc_jwt.description: For enterprise SSO sign-in, Logto bypasses its own MFA because the upstream IdP is treated as trusted.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag absence of Logto-side MFA challenge for enterprise SSO users as a bypass bug.

oidc_jwt.description: If direct sign-in cannot be completed because the connector is not found or not enabled, Logto redirects the user to the standard sign-in page.
oidc_jwt.note: Fallback to the hosted sign-in page is expected and should not be treated as state confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs retain their original scopes until expiration even after permissions are reduced.
oidc_jwt.note: This is standard JWT behavior; only newly issued tokens reflect downscoped permissions.

oidc_jwt.description: Signing out through the end-session flow revokes the centralized Logto session, but grants with `offline_access` may remain valid until grant TTL expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: Post-logout refresh success can be expected when offline_access-backed grants remain active.

oidc_jwt.description: Reusing the same JWT bearer token is generally allowed because Logto-issued JWT validation is stateless and RFC 7519 jti tracking is optional.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay of the same JWT as a vulnerability unless the tested context is explicitly one-time.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs keep previously granted scopes until they expire, even after user permissions are reduced.
oidc_jwt.note: Only newly issued tokens should be used to verify immediate permission reduction.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, newly granted permissions do not appear through refresh unless they were part of the original requested scope set; a new authorization flow may be required.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat missing newly-added scopes on refresh as a bug if they were not originally requested.

oidc_jwt.description: When no specific resource or organization is requested, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: Use introspection or userinfo for opaque tokens; lack of JWT claims is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs are not retroactively updated when permissions change; only newly issued tokens reflect RBAC changes.
oidc_jwt.note: A stale old token after role change is expected until expiration.

oidc_jwt.description: Enterprise SSO identities are automatically linked to an existing user account when the working email matches.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merge on matching email is documented behavior, not an accidental collision.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 audience-binding tests, the `resource` parameter in `/oidc/auth` and `/oidc/token` MUST exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator). Logto does not support wildcard or prefix matching for resource indicators; mismatched values produce the wrong audience or token type and invalidate the test.

For I5 scope-binding tests, requested `scope` values must exactly match permission names defined in Logto. Scope names are exact string matches only; prefixes or shortened names are not wildcards. Do NOT use partial scope names when testing authorization narrowing or escalation.

For JWT-based API tests, the fuzzer MUST request a `resource` parameter. If no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT. Using that opaque token in JWT-validation tests will cause false positives or wrong-path failures.

For organization-scoped JWT tests, include `organization_id` in the token request. Without `organization_id`, Logto evaluates only global roles/permissions and organization RBAC is not enforced, which would invalidate I5 organization-binding tests.

For organization token tests using authorization code flow, Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code exchange. The fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token, then call `/oidc/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token` plus organization parameters to obtain the organization JWT.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are BY DESIGN immutable. Permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens and never modify existing JWTs. A valid coherence test must compare newly issued tokens after config/role changes, not expect an already-issued JWT to change in place.

For I5 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, refresh cannot add scopes that were not requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. To test newly granted scopes, the fuzzer MUST run a new authorization flow rather than relying on refresh alone.

For I5 organization permission enlargement tests, new permissions can appear on next token issuance (refresh or token request), but only within the originally requested scope set. If the new permission was not in the original request, the fuzzer MUST start a new authorization flow.

For I2 expired/future token tests against Logto-issued JWTs, use a control token minted through the same flow with valid lifetime parameters and compare outcomes. A failed attack request without a valid control cannot distinguish token-time enforcement from broken client/app configuration.

For token exchange tests, the target application MUST have token exchange explicitly enabled. Token exchange is disabled by default; otherwise `/oidc/token` returns 'token exchange is not allowed for this application', which is a setup failure rather than a security result.

For PAT-based token exchange, set `subject_token_type=urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token`. For impersonation or access-token subject exchange, use the documented OAuth token type. Using the wrong subject token type causes exchange failure unrelated to the invariant under test.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, include the target `resource`/audience in the exchange request and verify the resulting token audience. Logto binds exchanged access tokens to the specified resource; omitting it may yield a token for a different audience or an opaque token, invalidating the test.

For `ui_locales`, matching is ordered exact language-tag selection against the tenant language library; Logto picks the first supported tag from the space-separated list. This parameter is not a wildcard matcher. Do not treat `ui_locales` as a pattern field in multi-identity tests.

For `first_screen`, `identifier`, and `direct_sign_in`, values are exact enumerated strings only. Unsupported values are ignored or fall back to the default sign-in page. Do not use wildcard-like values when testing flow coherence; fallback behavior is by design.

For direct sign-in tests, `direct_sign_in=social:<idp-name>` and `direct_sign_in=sso:<connector-id>` require exact connector identifiers. If the connector is missing or disabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page by design; this must not be reported as a flow-binding vulnerability.

For sign-out and freshness tests, end-session/global sign-out does not necessarily revoke grants when `offline_access` was granted. Refresh-token-capable grants may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. Do NOT assume browser sign-out alone invalidates all refresh-based reissuance.

Numeric sentinel: API resource token expiration time defaults to 3600 seconds when not configured. The docs do not define `0` as disable or literal zero. Never assume `0` disables expiry; use explicit positive values and verify actual token `exp`.

Numeric sentinel: one-time token `expiresIn` defaults to 600 seconds (10 minutes) when unspecified. The docs do not define `0` or negative values as disable sentinels. Never assume `0` means no expiry.

Numeric sentinel: Logto JWT validation examples in .NET use a default `ClockSkew` of 5 minutes in sample code, but this is application-side sample behavior, not a Logto server guarantee. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat a 5-minute grace period as a platform invariant when evaluating Logto itself.

For I2 freshness tests against `/oidc/token`, include a CONTROL token request/login alongside the attack case. A valid control should use a normal current-time token setup or standard client-credentials request so that rejection of the attack case can be distinguished from broken client/app/resource configuration.

Logto issues opaque access tokens when no specific `resource` or `organization_id` is included in the authorization request/token request. Opaque tokens are intended for `/oidc/me` and require `/oidc/token/introspection` for validation. They are not JWTs. For oidc_jwt tests that require JWT claim inspection or audience checks, the fuzzer MUST request a specific `resource` and/or `organization_id` so Logto returns a JWT instead of an opaque token.

Organization tokens cannot be fetched directly from the authorization code flow. To test organization-scoped JWTs, the fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token (authorization_code flow) and then call `/oidc/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token` plus `organization_id`, or use `grant_type=client_credentials` with `organization_id` for M2M scenarios.

For I5 organization authorization-binding tests, `organization_id` changes evaluation context. If omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated; organization RBAC is not enforced. Therefore any test expecting organization-scoped denial or grant MUST include the intended `organization_id` in the token request.

Default API resource behavior is special: if `resource` is omitted and a default API resource is configured, Logto may issue a JWT for that default audience when `openid` is not included, but may issue an opaque token for userinfo when `openid` is included. The fuzzer MUST control both `resource` and `scope` when testing audience binding to avoid false positives caused by default-audience fallback.

For I3 permission-change sequences, Logto JWTs are immutable after issuance. Permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens and never modify existing JWTs. A valid coherence test must compare NEW token issuance before vs. after the config/role change, not reuse an old token and expect its claims to change.

For I3 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, newly granted scopes will NOT appear through refresh unless they were part of the original requested scope set; to obtain newly granted scopes outside the original request, the client must run a new authorization flow. Do not treat missing newly-added scopes after refresh as a bug unless they were originally requested.

For I3 downscoping tests, Logto documents that newly issued tokens immediately reflect reduced scopes, but existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry. Do not flag an old still-valid JWT retaining old scopes as a violation; only new token issuance should be used as the oracle.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any RFC 8693 test (`token_exchange`, PAT exchange, impersonation-style exchange), the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled in application settings, otherwise failures are expected and not evidence of security enforcement.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, use `/oidc/token` with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` and explicitly set `resource`/target audience parameters for the destination API. Without an explicit target resource, the exchange result may reflect default audience behavior rather than proper audience binding.

For I2 replay tests, do NOT report reuse of the same JWT bearer token as a vulnerability by default. Logto documentation describes JWT validation as stateless and RFC 7519 `jti` tracking is optional. Replaying the same JWT without one-time semantics is a hardening check at most, not a security bug, except in one-time-token or other explicitly one-time contexts.

The one-time token (magic link) has a default expiration of 10 minutes if `expiresIn` is not specified. For timing tests around magic-link-derived flows, treat omitted expiry as a nonzero default rather than zero. Do not assume absence of `expiresIn` means immediate expiry or disabled expiry.

For I2 and I3 sign-out/revocation tests, revoking via `/oidc/token/revocation` revokes the specified token, but end-session/global sign-out does not necessarily revoke grants when `offline_access` is granted. Refresh-token/grant validity may continue until grant TTL expiry. Do not interpret successful refresh after browser sign-out as an automatic bug unless explicit revocation was performed.

Logto grant TTL defaults to 180 days for grants associated with `offline_access`. This is a numeric default sentinel-like behavior: absence of explicit grant revocation does NOT mean short-lived session semantics. Browser session termination and grant lifetime are separate. Tests must distinguish session logout from refresh-token/grant revocation.

For OIDC request-parameter tests (`ui_locales`, `login_hint`, `first_screen`, `identifier`, `direct_sign_in`), these are flow-shaping parameters only. If direct sign-in fails because connector is missing or disabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page by design. Do not treat fallback as state confusion or bypass.

Use `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` for `/oidc/token`, `/oidc/token/introspection`, and `/oidc/token/revocation`. Logto explicitly documents form encoding for direct OIDC API calls. Sending JSON may fail for protocol reasons unrelated to security behavior.

For I1 issuer-validation tests performed against Logto-issued JWTs in relying parties, issuer is fixed to `https://<your-logto-endpoint>/oidc` and not customizable. Tests that attempt to mutate issuer via tenant config are invalid for Logto as IdP; instead, verify relying-party enforcement against this fixed issuer value.

Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT when no resource is specified. For oidc_jwt tests, start_oidc_auth, exchange_code_for_token, login_with_jwt, or token_exchange MUST include a resource (or rely on a configured default API resource) to obtain a JWT access token; otherwise the returned access_token is opaque and only suitable for /oidc/me or introspection.

If a default API resource is configured, omitting resource does NOT mean 'no audience restriction': Logto will use the default API resource as the audience and issue a JWT for that audience. Tests for empty_audience or missing-resource behavior MUST control whether a default API resource exists, or results will be misinterpreted.

The resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator). There is no wildcard or pattern matching. For I5 audience tests, use exact URI equality; for negative tests, change the URI value, not formatting assumptions.

Scope names must exactly match the permission names defined for the API resource. No prefixes, shortened names, or wildcards are supported. For I5 authorization-binding tests, request exact scope strings and treat any partial name as a guaranteed mismatch, not a wildcard.

For organization-scoped JWT tests, organization RBAC is applied only when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. Tests comparing global vs organization authorization MUST vary organization_id explicitly.

Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. To test organization JWTs after interactive login, the sequence MUST obtain a refresh token first, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters. Do not expect exchange_code_for_token alone to return an organization token.

For global API resources, enlarged permissions do NOT appear through refresh unless they were already part of the originally requested scope set. A valid I3 permission-change test must distinguish between downscoping (visible in newly issued tokens) and enlarging permissions (may require a new authorization flow). Do NOT flag missing newly granted scopes after refresh as a broker bug if they were not in the original request.

For organization tokens, enlarged permissions appear on next issuance (refresh or token request) only within the originally requested scope set. I3 tests that tighten or enlarge organization permissions MUST request the candidate scopes up front, or the absence of scopes after refresh is inconclusive.

Permission changes never modify existing JWTs. Existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry; only newly issued tokens reflect changes. I3 tests for config or role changes MUST compare a fresh token issued after the change, not continued use of an old token.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise failures are expected configuration errors rather than security behavior.

PAT token exchange and refresh-token-derived access tokens are documented as equivalent in authorization behavior. I5 tests using token_exchange with subject_token_type=urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token should expect the same organization/resource/scope semantics as refresh-token issuance, differing only in initial grant type.

The token endpoint accepts both confidential-client authentication (HTTP Basic with client_id:client_secret) and public-client style client_id in the form body for some flows. Tests must use the authentication mode appropriate to the application type; a missing client_secret on a confidential client is a setup failure, not a protocol weakness.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against JWT validation in protected APIs, include a control token that is valid now (e.g., exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}). Without a control, a 401 may reflect broken JWKS/issuer setup rather than freshness enforcement.

Logto validation examples verify issuer automatically but often leave audience verification to application logic (verify_aud false / manual audience checks). For I5 audience-binding tests, the protected API under test MUST explicitly validate aud/resource and, for organization APIs, organization_id as well; otherwise audience-mismatch acceptance is by application misconfiguration, not necessarily Logto token issuance behavior.

OIDC discovery is available at /oidc/.well-known/openid-configuration and exposes issuer and jwks_uri. I1 trust-anchor and key-rotation tests MUST derive issuer/JWKS from the same tenant endpoint under test; hardcoded mismatched issuer or JWKS values will create false failures.

Logto signing key rotation for Cloud takes effect immediately, but rotating keys consecutively can invalidate all issued tokens. I3 key-rotation tests MUST perform a single rotation step and then test old-vs-new key acceptance; do not chain multiple rotations in one sequence.

For OSS deployments, after rotating signing keys a Logto instance restart is required before the new key takes effect. I3 key-rotation tests on OSS MUST include restart/synchronization handling or they will observe stale trust state.

Current SDK sign-out behavior is global sign-out: it redirects to /session/end and confirms logout, revoking the centralized Logto session. However, if offline_access was granted, the app grant is not revoked by end-session and refresh-token-based authorization may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. Do NOT treat successful refresh after browser sign-out as an automatic I3/I2 violation.

Grant TTL default is 180 days. End-session does not necessarily revoke grants with offline_access. Freshness or revocation tests that expect immediate invalidation of all tokens after sign-out MUST explicitly revoke the token/grant or avoid offline_access, otherwise continued token exchange/refresh can be by design.

Logto supports PKCE and the token endpoint expects code_verifier for authorization_code exchanges. OIDC flow coherence tests must bind start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token with the same code_challenge/code_verifier pair and same redirect_uri; otherwise failures are normal protocol enforcement.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
